newsitem.title: CHINA: Gulfstream to expand sales into China.
newsitem.headline: Gulfstream to expand sales into China.

text.p: U.S. business aircraft maker Gulfstream is seeking access to airports in China to boost its corporate profile in the country.
"We are beginning dialogue with the proper authorities to discuss access to airports in China," Bryan T. Moss, vice chairman of Gulfstream, told a news conference on Friday.
"We want to have chance to compete in China, opportunities are tremendous," Moss said, adding it was too early to disclose the company's anticipated sales and investment in China.
He said access to Chinese airports was difficult to obtain but essential to sales in China. Expanding the sales of its business jet aircraft in China was a long-term project, he said.

About 75 percent of the Savannah, Georgia-based company's market is in the United States. But Gulfstream expects its international market will grow to 50 percent of its sales in the next four to six years, he said without elaborating.
